content: Deutetrabenazine metabolism is influenced by hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. When co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, the dose of deutetrabenazine should not exceed 18 mg per dose and 36 mg per day. Ritonavir increases dexamethasone levels or effects by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, dexamethasone decreases ritonavir levels or effects through the same mechanism. Ritonavir also increases dexamethasone levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. DHEA (herbal supplement) increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored, and alternatives should be considered if available. Ritonavir also increases the levels or effects of buccal and intranasal diazepam through the same mechanism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Ritonavir enhances the effects of diazoxide through other mechanisms, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir and didanosine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Ritonavir decreases didanosine levels or effects by increasing gastric pH, applicable only to the oral forms of both agents. Didanosine should be taken one hour before or two hours after lopinavir/ritonavir oral solution administration. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. Ritonavir increases digoxin levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by reducing renal and hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. Diltiazem increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and ritonavir increases diltiazem levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases docetaxel levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases dofetilide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored, and alternatives should be considered if available. There is an increased risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Ritonavir increases doravirine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases doxepin levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir also increases the levels or effects of doxepin cream through CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir increases doxorubicin levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. The same applies to liposomal doxorubicin. Ritonavir increases dronabinol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Dronedarone increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases duloxetine levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases duvelisib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored, as co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib AUC, potentially raising the risk of toxicities. Efavirenz decreases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. Elagolix increases ritonavir levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and decreases ritonavir levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored if co-administered. Dose adjustments may be necessary. Ritonavir increases eletriptan levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Eliglustat increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Therapeutic drug concentrations should be monitored, or the dosage of concomitant drugs should be reduced and titrated to clinical effect. Ritonavir increases eluxadoline levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution is advised when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Ritonavir increases elvitegravir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. Encorafenib affects CYP3A4 metabolism and both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may increase toxicity or reduce efficacy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage, and MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Monitor closely for signs of toxicity. Ritonavir and enfuvirtide both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases erlotinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) increases ritonavir levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases escitalopram levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity and the risk of serotonin syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases esomeprazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases estradiol levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and toxicities. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases eszopiclone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored, and the starting dose of eszopiclone should be reduced to 1 mg/day. Ritonavir increases ethosuximide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases etonogestrel levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases etoposide levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases etravirine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir decreases the effects of exenatide (injectable solution and suspension) through other mechanisms, with reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ezogabine and ritonavir both increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. QT interval monitoring is recommended, especially when ezogabine is titrated to 1200 mg/day. Fedratinib increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP2D6 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases felodipine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while felodipine increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases fesoterodine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Fluconazole increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases fludrocortisone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Fludrocortisone decreases ritonavir levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases flunisolide (inhaled) levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases flurazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored, and alternatives should be considered if available. Lowering the benzodiazepine dose may be necessary. Ritonavir increases fluticasone levels or effects (both furoate and inhaled forms) by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases fluvastatin toxicity through other mechanisms, with OATP1B1 inhibitors potentially increasing the risk of myopathy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Fluvoxamine increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Fosamprenavir increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Fosaprepitant increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Fosphenytoin decreases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases fostamatinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrate drugs, and dosage reductions may be required. Garlic decreases ritonavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases gefitinib levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored, as strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Ritonavir increases gentamicin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases ritonavir levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir may increase or decrease glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide levels. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors have been noted. Alternatives should be considered if available. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Grapefruit increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Griseofulvin decreases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases guanfacine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, the dosage should be reduced to half the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Ritonavir increases haloperidol levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases hydrocodone levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Ritonavir increases hydrocortisone levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Hydrocortisone decreases ritonavir levels through the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases hydromorphone levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir decreases ifosfamide levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism but increases its effects by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP2B6 inducers may increase ifosfamide metabolism to its active metabolite. Monitor for increased effects or toxicities. Ritonavir increases iloperidone levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs eliminated by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases imatinib levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Ritonavir increases imipramine levels or effects by affecting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases indacaterol levels (inhaled) through modulation of P-gp and CYP3A4 activities. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Indinavir increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir decreases the effects of insulin (various forms) through pharmacodynamic antagonism or other mechanisms. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Ritonavir decreases isavuconazonium sulfate levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Isoniazid increases ritonavir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases istradefylline levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Istradefylline increases ritonavir levels through the same mechanisms. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 and P-gp substrates in clinical trials. Dose reduction of sensitive substrates should be considered. Ritonavir increases itraconazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit itraconazole dose to 200 mg/day in patients receiving ritonavir. Therapy should be adjusted or closely monitored. Ritonavir increases ivacaftor levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce ivacaftor dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ivacaftor increases ritonavir levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
